claims.explanation: Ouabain is a cardiac glycoside that binds and inhibits the Na+/K+-ATPase (ATP1A1), and its selectivity likely reflects dependence on specific ATP1A1/ATP1A3 isoform expression and on HIF-1-driven survival signaling, since cardiac glycosides block HIF-1alpha synthesis. Lines with high ATP1A1 expression and/or HIF-1 pathway activation are expected to be more sensitive, while those expressing the relatively ouabain-resistant ATP1A2 isoform or lacking HIF-1 dependence would be protected.

VHL loss activates HIF-1 independent of translation, reducing dependence on HIF-1alpha synthesis
